title: Japan PM wants Asia oil security task force created
summary: Japan proposed yesterday the creation of the Asia oil security task force that would coordinate cooperation on oil stockpiling and release of supplies during emergencies as countries seek to mitigate…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Japan proposed yesterday the creation of the Asia oil security task force that would coordinate cooperation on oil stockpiling and release of supplies during emergencies as countries seek to mitigate the impacts of oil supply disruptions stemming from the Middle East crisis.

Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae introduced the initiative at the 4th Asia Zero-Emission Community (AZEC) leaders’ meeting during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Pasay City.
“I also wish to propose an initiative for cooperation on oil stockpiling in Asia through the use of idle tanks in Japan,” Takaichi, who chaired the AZEC with President Marcos, said in her remarks.
The Asia oil security task force will be Asia’s equivalent to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the Japanese leader said.
Established in 1974 following the oil crisis in 1973, IEA requires member-countries to stockpile oil equivalent to 90 days of consumption.
Takaichi said the initiative would be coordinated with the Philippines-led joint stockpiling scheme.
She called for the strengthening of the Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience (POWERR) Asia, announced this year, evolving the existing AZEC into AZEC 2.0.
Takaichi also proposed the “POWERR Gulf Initiative,” which aims to strengthen coordination between oil-producing countries and energy-consuming countries in Asia.
“Japan will serve as the nexus connecting oil-producing countries in Asia,” she said.
Marcos, for his part, said disruptions along critical supply routes, such as the Strait of Hormuz, “never stay local.”
“They reverberate across global supply chains. As I emphasized at the AZEC Plus Online Summit, no single nation can insulate itself from shocks of this magnitude by acting alone,” he said.
Marcos said the Philippines was making progress on its strategic petroleum reserve and is seeking investments in energy projects to achieve regional energy security.
“But stockpiling is not enough. Sustainable and enduring energy security demands that oil consuming and oil producing nations act in unison,” he said.
“We must deepen information sharing and practical storage arrangements, as well as commit to upholding international law to keep sea lanes open and maintain fair, transparent markets,” Marcos said.
He proposed a regional study on joint oil stockpiling to strengthen energy security at the AZEC Plus online summit in April.
AZEC is a Japan-led initiative aimed at promoting clean energy, reducing carbon emissions and supporting sustainable economic growth while strengthening energy security across the region.
AZEC members include Japan, the Philippines, Australia, Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

“Under this POWERR Asia initiative, we are going to provide assistance to construct for example to stockpile, providing facilities of crude oil, or support, provide capacity, building assistance, or share the expertise in order to establish system of a stockpiling, not only the facility itself, but also the system as a whole,” Japanese Foreign Ministry Press Secretary Toshihiro Kitamura told journalists at a separate press briefing.
AI safety
Takaichi also launched the Japan-ASEAN Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety and Security Partnership to respond to emerging risks of cybersecurity threats and loss of human control over AI.
The Japan-ASEAN AI Safety and Security Partnership is part of efforts to expand the Japan-ASEAN Co-Creation Initiative for AI.

“As a trusted partner of ASEAN, Japan will support ASEAN member-states to build AI safety governance capabilities suited to their national circumstances, thereby co-creating a safe, secure and trustworthy AI ecosystem and enhancing its resilience, through the following lines of efforts,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan said in a statement.
The partnership will be implemented in coordination with the ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance and the ASEAN AI Safety Network. — Pia Lee-Brago
